text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions. For example, a variable called `userAge` is much better than `x`. Functions should also be short and do only one job, which makes them easier to test and reuse. When code is clean, it becomes easier to maintain. Other developers can fix bugs or add new features without feeling confused. In short, writing clean code saves time and helps teams work together more effectively.
